\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عمارة} (ʿimāra)}{عمارة (ʿimāra)}]{\ar{عمارة} (ʿimāra) — a block of flats; architecture}

\label{lesson:AR-C454-imara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to get back, then the Arabic for a meter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عمارة}}
\textbf{\ar{عمارة}} — \emph{ʿimāra} — \textquotedblleft{}a block of flats; architecture\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نسكن} \ar{في} \ar{عمارة} \ar{قديمة} \ar{في} \ar{وسط} \ar{المدينة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{naskunu fī ʿimāra qadīma fī wasaṭ al-madīna.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We live in an old block of flats in the city centre.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عمارة}} (\emph{ʿimāra}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-m-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to inhabit, to build up\textquotedblright{} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿimāra}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿimāra}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naskunu fī ʿimāra qadīma fī wasaṭ al-madīna.} — We live in an old block of flats in the city centre.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to get back, then the Arabic for a meter, then say \emph{ʿimāra} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{عمارة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A block of flats; architecture\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ناطحة} \ar{سحاب} (nāṭiḥat saḥāb)}{ناطحة سحاب (nāṭiḥat saḥāb)}]{\ar{ناطحة} \ar{سحاب} (nāṭiḥat saḥāb) — a skyscraper}

\label{lesson:AR-C454-natihat-sahab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a meter, then the Arabic for a block of flats.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ناطحة} \ar{سحاب}}
\textbf{\ar{ناطحة} \ar{سحاب}} — \emph{nāṭiḥat saḥāb} — \textquotedblleft{}a skyscraper\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{رأينا} \ar{ناطحة} \ar{سحاب} \ar{من} \ar{نافذة} \ar{الفندق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{raʾaynā nāṭiḥat saḥāb min nāfidhat al-funduq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We saw a skyscraper from the hotel window.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ناطحة} \ar{سحاب}} (\emph{nāṭiḥat saḥāb}) is a modern coinage built from two native Arabic words (Lane gives both roots): \emph{nāṭiḥa}, \textquotedblleft{}one that butts\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{n-ṭ-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to butt with the horns\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{saḥāb}, \textquotedblleft{}clouds\textquotedblright{}. It is a calque of English \emph{skyscraper}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nāṭiḥat saḥāb}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nāṭiḥat saḥāb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{raʾaynā nāṭiḥat saḥāb min nāfidhat al-funduq.} — We saw a skyscraper from the hotel window.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a meter, then the Arabic for a block of flats, then say \emph{nāṭiḥat saḥāb} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ناطحة} \ar{سحاب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A skyscraper\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ضاحية} (ḍāḥiya)}{ضاحية (ḍāḥiya)}]{\ar{ضاحية} (ḍāḥiya) — a suburb}

\label{lesson:AR-C454-dahiya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a block of flats, then the Arabic for a skyscraper.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ضاحية}}
\textbf{\ar{ضاحية}} — \emph{ḍāḥiya} — \textquotedblleft{}a suburb\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يسكن} \ar{عمي} \ar{في} \ar{ضاحية} \ar{بعيدة} \ar{عن} \ar{المركز}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaskunu ʿammī fī ḍāḥiya baʿīda ʿan al-markaz.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My uncle lives in a suburb far from the centre.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ضاحية}} (\emph{ḍāḥiya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḍ-ḥ-w}, \textquotedblleft{}to be in the sun; to come into view\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives \emph{ḍāḥiya} as the outer, exposed side or tract of a place; \emph{ḍuḥā}, \textquotedblleft{}late morning\textquotedblright{}, shares the root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍāḥiya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍāḥiya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yaskunu ʿammī fī ḍāḥiya baʿīda ʿan al-markaz.} — My uncle lives in a suburb far from the centre.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a block of flats, then the Arabic for a skyscraper, then say \emph{ḍāḥiya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ضاحية} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A suburb\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مسبح} (masbaḥ)}{مسبح (masbaḥ)}]{\ar{مسبح} (masbaḥ) — a swimming pool}

\label{lesson:AR-C454-masbah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a skyscraper, then the Arabic for a suburb.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مسبح}}
\textbf{\ar{مسبح}} — \emph{masbaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a swimming pool\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سبح} \ar{الأطفال} \ar{في} \ar{مسبح} \ar{الفندق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sabaḥa al-aṭfāl fī masbaḥ al-funduq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children swam in the hotel pool.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مسبح}} (\emph{masbaḥ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-b-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to swim\textquotedblright{} (Lane). The pattern \emph{mafʿal} makes it the place of swimming.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{masbaḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{masbaḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sabaḥa al-aṭfāl fī masbaḥ al-funduq.} — The children swam in the hotel pool.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a skyscraper, then the Arabic for a suburb, then say \emph{masbaḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مسبح} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A swimming pool\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مجمع} \ar{تجاري} (mujammaʿ tijārī)}{مجمع تجاري (mujammaʿ tijārī)}]{\ar{مجمع} \ar{تجاري} (mujammaʿ tijārī) — a shopping centre}

\label{lesson:AR-C454-mujammaa-tijari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a suburb, then the Arabic for a swimming pool.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مجمع} \ar{تجاري}}
\textbf{\ar{مجمع} \ar{تجاري}} — \emph{mujammaʿ tijārī} — \textquotedblleft{}a shopping centre\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اشترينا} \ar{الملابس} \ar{من} \ar{مجمع} \ar{تجاري} \ar{كبير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ishtaraynā al-malābis min mujammaʿ tijārī kabīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We bought the clothes at a big shopping centre.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مجمع} \ar{تجاري}} (\emph{mujammaʿ tijārī}) is built from two native Arabic words: \emph{mujammaʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}a place where things are gathered\textquotedblright{}, on the root \emph{j-m-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to gather\textquotedblright{} (Lane), and \emph{tijārī}, \textquotedblleft{}of trade\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{t-j-r} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mujammaʿ tijārī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ishtaraynā al-malābis min mujammaʿ tijārī kabīr.} — We bought the clothes at a big shopping centre.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a suburb, then the Arabic for a swimming pool, then say \emph{mujammaʿ tijārī} again

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 447–454 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R454-review-447-454}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for a shower and a clothes iron.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a shower, a clothes iron, a dryer, to break down, to check on
  \item noise, to disturb, to wake, to calm down, to complain
  \item a complaint, compensation, to compensate, to grumble, to swap
  \item a town hall, a consulate, working hours, a line of people, to apply
  \item a police station, a library, to enquire, to check over, to ban
  \item a branch office, a balance, a money transfer, to change money, to deposit
  \item an instalment, in cash, a cash machine, to get back, a meter
  \item a block of flats, a skyscraper, a suburb, a swimming pool, a shopping centre
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A shower? (\textbf{\ar{دش}}, \emph{dush}.) A clothes iron? (\textbf{\ar{مكواة}}, \emph{mikwāh}.) A dryer? (\textbf{\ar{مجفف}}, \emph{mujaffif}.) To break down? (\textbf{\ar{تعطل}}, \emph{taʿaṭṭala}.) To check on? (\textbf{\ar{تفقد}}, \emph{tafaqqada}.) Noise? (\textbf{\ar{ضجيج}}, \emph{ḍajīj}.) To disturb? (\textbf{\ar{أزعج}}, \emph{azʿaja}.) To wake? (\textbf{\ar{أيقظ}}, \emph{ayqaẓa}.) To calm down? (\textbf{\ar{هدأ}}, \emph{hadaʾa}.) To complain? (\textbf{\ar{اشتكى}}, \emph{ishtakā}.) A complaint? (\textbf{\ar{شكوى}}, \emph{shakwā}.) Compensation? (\textbf{\ar{تعويض}}, \emph{taʿwīḍ}.) To compensate? (\textbf{\ar{عوض}}, \emph{ʿawwaḍa}.) To grumble? (\textbf{\ar{تذمر}}, \emph{tadhammara}.) To swap? (\textbf{\ar{استبدل}}, \emph{istabdala}.) A town hall? (\textbf{\ar{بلدية}}, \emph{baladiyya}.) A consulate? (\textbf{\ar{قنصلية}}, \emph{qunṣuliyya}.) Working hours? (\textbf{\ar{دوام}}, \emph{dawām}.) A line of people? (\textbf{\ar{طابور}}, \emph{ṭābūr}.) To apply? (\textbf{\ar{تقدم}}, \emph{taqaddama}.) A police station? (\textbf{\ar{مخفر}}, \emph{makhfar}.) A library? (\textbf{\ar{مكتبة}}, \emph{maktaba}.) To enquire? (\textbf{\ar{استفسر}}, \emph{istafsara}.) To check over? (\textbf{\ar{راجع}}, \emph{rājaʿa}.) To ban? (\textbf{\ar{حظر}}, \emph{ḥaẓara}.) A branch office? (\textbf{\ar{فرع}}, \emph{farʿ}.) A balance? (\textbf{\ar{رصيد}}, \emph{raṣīd}.) A money transfer? (\textbf{\ar{حوالة}}, \emph{ḥawāla}.) To change money? (\textbf{\ar{صرف}}, \emph{ṣarafa}.) To deposit? (\textbf{\ar{أودع}}, \emph{awdaʿa}.) An instalment? (\textbf{\ar{قسط}}, \emph{qisṭ}.) In cash? (\textbf{\ar{نقدا}}, \emph{naqdan}.) A cash machine? (\textbf{\ar{صراف} \ar{آلي}}, \emph{ṣarrāf ālī}.) To get back? (\textbf{\ar{استرد}}, \emph{istaradda}.) A meter? (\textbf{\ar{عداد}}, \emph{ʿaddād}.) A block of flats? (\textbf{\ar{عمارة}}, \emph{ʿimāra}.) A skyscraper? (\textbf{\ar{ناطحة} \ar{سحاب}}, \emph{nāṭiḥat saḥāb}.) A suburb? (\textbf{\ar{ضاحية}}, \emph{ḍāḥiya}.) A swimming pool? (\textbf{\ar{مسبح}}, \emph{masbaḥ}.) A shopping centre? (\textbf{\ar{مجمع} \ar{تجاري}}, \emph{mujammaʿ tijārī}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
